The document below is the pipeline run end to end. It is a single reproducible
R Markdown file: one configuration block at the top switches it between a binary
and a continuous outcome, and expensive steps are cached so that re-running after
an edit takes seconds rather than hours.

:::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple"}
It is a large document with its own table of contents. Open it in a new tab and
use the sidebar to move between parts.
::::

[Open the full analysis →](output/full-analysis.html){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"}

## What is in it

| Part | Contents |
|---|---|
| **Setup** | Package installation, source files, caching, and the single configuration block that drives everything else |
| **I. Fit-the-fit** | BART estimation of per-patient CATEs; CART for subgroup discovery; variable importance and interaction (VIVI) heatmaps |
| **II. Sensitivity** | A grid over the BART prior specification, and cross-method comparison against Bayesian Causal Forest and gradient boosting |
| **III. Prognostic score** | Treatment effect heterogeneity by baseline risk, with the prognostic score estimated three ways |
| **IV. ITE quantiles** | Randomization-based one- and two-sided confidence limits, the benefiting-fraction bounds, and a second worked example on a continuous outcome |

::: {.callout-important appearance="simple"}
Results shown on individual patient data are subject to each trial's data use
agreement. The source code is openly available so the method can be applied
elsewhere.
:::
